title: T5 hallway: the door registry
purpose: Every door in the hallway: what question it answers, where it is, and how fresh it is. A door is a documented, versioned, reachable entry point onto one part of the program. This registry exists because the design names a hallway whose job is navigation, and a hallway with no door inventory is a corridor.
why_a_registry_and_not_a_list: The design record already carried a ten-row door table by hand, and within one session that table's own category grew: two more doors were demanded by the design, and seven more were built for the retrieval, spec and gate work. Hand-maintained tables do not survive that. Worse, the design's own audit found a reader-facing document disagreeing with three separately-asserted implementations, and a stale Heartbeat size that the code comments already said was fixed. Documentation drift here is not cosmetic, so freshness is CHECKED by tools/door_lint.py rather than asserted.

state_legend.CURRENT: Verified against the code it describes.
state_legend.PARTLY_FIXED: Some claims verified, some known wrong. Treat the wrong parts as absent.
state_legend.STALE: Known not to match the code. Read only for what is uniquely valuable in it.
state_legend.SUPERSEDED: Replaced, but retained because it uniquely holds something nothing else does.
state_legend.BUILT: Created 2026-09-30 as part of the retrieval and spec work.

doors.question: How is a multi-step job choreographed, with what preconditions and rollback
doors.notes: A plan is not a script. It declares goal, context, invariants required, phases in a fixed order, what verifies each phase, and what to do on failure. The separation matters because a plan can be reviewed and diffed while an orchestrator stays small and boring.

doors.question: What has each plan actually done, and where did it stop
doors.notes: Executes plans. Enforces preconditions, verifies every phase, halts on first failure and prints the rollback. Allowlists what a plan may name, so a plan cannot invoke an arbitrary command. Records an append-only transcript. Deliberately does not reorder, parallelise, retry or decide -- an orchestrator that decides for itself is a script wearing a plan's clothes.

doors.question: What changed between gate runs, and when
doors.notes: The conversational counterpart to the one-way gates. Speaks ONLY on change, writes runs/watch/gate-history.jsonl, and answers --since and --why. A gate that talks constantly is a gate nobody reads, so silence is the normal case and is not a failure to report.

doors.question: How are materials, impacts and footstep records actually laid out
doors.notes: Engine-derived from CommonLibF4, with static_assert sizes: MATT is BGSMaterialType at sizeof 0x80, FSTP is BGSFootstep at 0x30, IPCT is BGSImpactData. Corrects an incoming Skyrim-flavoured reference on three points and records that four of its proposed struct fields do not exist in the engine at all.

doors.question: How does a bit become a file, in each paradigm
doors.notes: Seven rungs mapped across native, Python and Creation Engine. The CE column is CORRECTED: CE has four rungs where the ladder has seven, no arrays of records, no 2D grids in a plugin, and the file rung carries a master/override dimension no memory paradigm has. Also records the struct padding arithmetic that a proposed zero-copy design got wrong.

doors.question: What is actually stopping us, sorted by what unblocks it soonest
doors.notes: AUTHORITATIVE VERSION. Supersedes ai_context/spec/blockers_to_environment.json, which stays on disk unedited (tasks/roadmap/VERSIONING.md, Class B); version 1's `critical_path_to_a_cell_on_disk` read [B1,B2,B3] while four records carried blocks_the_critical_path true, so it contradicted itself and the array was the error. B1-B4 are the whole critical path to a testable environment and all four are tractable today. B5, Layer A, is the most important open question in the project and is NOT on that path -- it blocks using the environment in-game, not creating it. BRANCH ON blocks_the_critical_path, a real boolean on all eight records; do NOT branch on `status`, which is still free prose. Version 2 records why no closed vocabulary was invented (status-vocabulary changes are F2.1b, the owner's decision) and shows that the two existing closed sets measure a different axis. No keeper is named and no lint checks this file, which is why the internal contradiction survived: it is an invariant nothing enforces.

doors.question: What are the parts of this program, what proves each one, and what does each take over
doors.notes: AUTHORITATIVE VERSION. Supersedes ai_context/spec/program_components.json, which stays on disk unedited as the record of the state before the replacement map existed (tasks/roadmap/VERSIONING.md, Class B). Version 2 adds a `replaces` array to all 14 entries and moves the Creation Kit out of a `role` string into `replaces`, where a program can join it; the map's own NOT_PLANNED verdict for the CK sits in the same entry's notes. Read `replaces` together with `notes`: the array names the JOB a component takes over, not coverage it has, and 7 of the 14 are explicitly empty because the map is PRODUCT level. CAUTION, found 2026-10-03 and NOT fixed here because it is another agent's file: spec_lint's honesty rule for gate_covered does not execute. The bucket/available block at tools/spec_lint.py:189-200 is indented to the level of the entry loop, so the check at line 203 sits inside the `available` branch and no entry in the spec layer has an `available` field. Masked proof: status set to `absent` with gate_covered true, lint stayed GREEN at exit 0. So this file's booleans are honest by hand, not by gate.

doors.question: Which legacy product do we replace, how, and what do we add beyond parity
doors.notes: PRODUCT level, 31 rows, one per legacy Fallout 4 mod-tooling product: 1 COVERED, 2 DECLARED, 14 PLANNED, 5 DIFFERENT_MECHANISM, 8 NOT_PLANNED, 1 REJECTED. By host: 19 need no game and no editor, 8 need the game, 4 need the CK, so 'the program runs without either host' is countable rather than aspirational. The capability-level companion is the `compat` door above and the two granularities are not interchangeable. Read `requires_host` before quoting this file as a scope statement. Added as a door on 2026-10-03: the map existed with no way in from here, which is the exact failure this registry exists to prevent.

doors.question: What surfaces exist, by kind and direction, and which are actually proven
doors.notes: Seven kinds, and lumping them together is how a working mechanism gets mistaken for a working feature: OPERATOR, AI, ENGINE_PROGRAM, ENGINE_MOD, PROVIDER_SOURCE, CREATION, CROSS. Audited 2026-09-30 by smoke-testing each surface rather than reading its intent. Its own closed status vocabulary is MET / PARTIALLY_MET / DECLARED / NOT_MET / UNVERIFIED. Known drift, found 2026-10-03, NOT fixed here: three surfaces carry evidence strings quoting '106 python checks pass' and the real number is 108, so this file is the wrong side of that drift and the two evidence strings should be corrected by whoever owns it.

doors.question: Which preconditions each side of the work requires, and is each one actually met
doors.notes: Three sides: engine, in-house, creation-kit. An invariant is not a capability -- it is true or it is not, and while it is false the whole side is unavailable, which is why a global green gate is never allowed to imply a working side. The engine side fails at exactly one invariant, Layer A, and that single failure is why S0 is unproven. Known drift, found 2026-10-03, NOT fixed here: the file declares status_vocabulary MET / NOT_MET / UNVERIFIED / NOT_APPLICABLE and then uses PARTIALLY_MET in three entries, which is the value this registry's own sibling surfaces.json declares. Nothing enforces either vocabulary, so the leak is silent.

doors.question: What can a human or an agent actually DO here, and what observable proves it
doors.notes: 23 capabilities in 9 groups, each with requires, exercise and evidence. The separation it enforces is ACHIEVED versus merely discussed: a task group moves capabilities from BLOCKED to AVAILABLE and the newly available set is how you know the task worked. tools/taskrun.ps1 computes $missing from `requires` and blocks, which makes this the only genuinely ENFORCED requires field in the repository -- contrast ai_context/plans/schema.json, which declares the same field and whose enforcement only prints. No keeper is named because no linter checks this file. Known gap, found 2026-10-03 and NOT fixable by me: there is NO provenance field anywhere in this file, which breaks the project's non-negotiable that a fact with no provenance may not exist, and runtime.layerA's exercise field literally reads '(not built -- needs a BSScript declaration in method order)', so a capability can be listed with no way to run it.

doors.question: What is the smallest test facility that can answer S0, one step at a time
doors.notes: Steps are added ONE AT A TIME between runs, because a group that must be written all at once before anything can run will not get written. Resume is decided by the checks and never by the journal, so a Creation Kit crash costs at most the step in flight. Each step names what it unlocks, which is the join into the `capabilities` door above. No keeper is named: nothing lints this file, and its checkpoint path is inside the game Data folder, which is outside the project.

doors.question: Which plugins load in a CK session, and which are excluded on purpose
doors.notes: The curated 'core' profile: 35 entries plus 5 documented exclusions, each with a reason. It is deliberately not maximal, because every master is load time and crash surface in the CK -- and the CK has three crash dumps on record. SimSettlements 2 is excluded BY DECISION to resolve the workshop-hook conflict rather than defer it, which is the difference between excluding and forgetting. After a load, read EditorWarnings.txt for missing masters: that is how a curated list gets corrected rather than guessed at. No keeper is named; nothing lints this file.
